title: Measuring and Decomposing Mode Separation via the Canonical Diffusion
claim: A label-free, barrier-sensitive measure tracks mode separation like mutual information, and captures structure that entropy and variance-based PCA miss.
layout: 6 panels in 2x3 grid; four dual-axis line plots, two 2D scatter panels
description: A 2x3 grid of plots. The left two-thirds hold four dual-axis line charts, (a) to (d). Each charts SSA as a solid blue line with a shaded ±1 SD band on the left axis. MI is a dashed red line with square markers on the right axis. The x-axes sweep separation, variance, weight and number of modes. In (a), SSA stays flat and then shoots up while MI saturates. In (b) and (c), both curves fall. In (d), both rise, and daggered points mark the K=4,5 results. A legend sits in the lower left of (c). The right third holds two 2D scatter plots with gray points and contour ellipses. Panel (e) shows an isotropic Gaussian with short blue DA1 and red PC1 arrows. Panel (f) shows two parallel flat ellipses. There, the blue DA1 arrow points between the modes and the red PC1 arrow runs horizontally. Text boxes in the corners give the SSA and entropy values.
caption: Two readouts of the canonical diffusion. (a--d) SSA on 10D GMMs (left 2/3): SSA (blue, left axis) and MI (red, right axis) across sweeps in (a) mode separation, (b) isotropic variance at fixed separation, (c) weight asymmetry, (d) mode count. SSA tracks MI in ordering; MI saturates near $H(Z) = \log k$ while SSA grows with barrier height. Mean over $10$ seeds, $\pm 1$ SD. Daggered points ($K{=}4,5$) did not meet the $1/N$ criterion at $T_{\mathrm{phys}}=200$\,s; since $\rho^2 \ge 0$, truncation makes $\hat S$ a lower bound on the population value (ordering preserved, Appendix [ref]). (e--f) DA vs.\ PCA on 2D distributions (right 1/3): (e) isotropic $\mathcal{N}(0, 25\,I_2)$, $H = 6.06$, SSA$\,=1.022$: no population direction, arrows reflect finite-sample noise. (f) Parallel ellipses, means $(0, \mp 3)$, covariances $\mathrm{diag}(25, 1)$, $H = 5.14$, SSA$\,=1.822$: entropy ranks (e) above (f); SSA inverts. DA1 points between modes; PC1 along max variance. DA1 passes anisotropic-null and dip tests ($p < 10^{-3}$); PC1 fails dip ($p = 0.99$). Details: Appendices [ref], [ref]; snapshots: Figure [ref].
abstract: Mode separation, namely how sharply a distribution fragments into barrier-separated clusters, is a fundamental geometric property of densities, difficult to quantify in high dimensions. Modes are often the meaningful alternatives in the data, such as the conformations of a molecule or the distinct semantic types among a generative model's outputs. Mode separation is distinct from dispersion, which is what standard label-free tools capture: differential entropy rises with spread regardless of fragmentation, and PCA orders directions by variance regardless of barriers. Mutual information does capture it, but only given the latent component labels, which are usually unavailable. We measure mode separation through a single stochastic process intrinsic to the density, namely the unique reversible diffusion with $f$ as its stationary distribution and a constant scalar diffusion coefficient. From its autocovariance matrix we extract two readouts. The first, SSA (Sum of Squared Autocorrelations), is a scalar barrier-sensitive measure. The second, DA (Dominant Autocorrelation directions), gives linear projections ordered by metastability rather than variance. Under an isotropic-Gaussian null, we derive the limiting spectrum of the empirical autocovariance in closed form, generalizing the Marchenko--Pastur law. Its upper edge gives a noise floor that separates metastable directions from sampling noise. Both readouts use only samples and a score function, scaling to high dimensions through pretrained score-based generative models via Tweedie's identity. We apply our framework to three settings: (i) synthetic Gaussian mixtures, where SSA tracks mutual information; (ii) SDXL text-to-image generations, where SSA and DA capture structure that entropy and PCA miss; and (iii) molecular dynamics of alanine dipeptide, where DA recovers the known slow backbone dihedrals from static samples alone.
